theme: 中国茶文化在当代社交中的分享

evidence_used.statement: UNESCO inscribed China's Spring Festival social practices on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2024, highlighting family reunion, community harmony and cultural continuity.
CGTN reports that Spring Festival social practices were inscribed on UNESCO's ICH Representative List in 2024 and are increasingly shared worldwide.
UNESCO recognizes China's traditional tea processing techniques and social practices (2022); tea producers developed six main tea categories plus reprocessed teas, with over 2,000 products.

five_w.who: A lifestyle and wellness influencer who loves aesthetic drink rituals and global cafe culture.
five_w.says_what: China's UNESCO-recognized traditional tea processing features 6 main categories and over 2,000 varieties, offering a vibrant social ritual beyond a simple daily drink.
five_w.channel: Instagram: short, visual-friendly, emoji-rich, and scroll-stopping with a POV hook.
five_w.to_whom: Americans who love daily iced coffee runs and cafe-hopping; bridging their love for aesthetic drink routines with China's historic tea social vibes.
five_w.effect: Spark curiosity about the diversity of Chinese tea categories and invite interactive sharing.

post: POV: Your daily iced coffee just got a massive upgrade. 🍵✨ Did you know China’s traditional tea processing is UNESCO-recognized? It’s not just one drink—it’s 6 main categories and over 2,000 varieties! 🌿 From cozy oolong gatherings to vibrant green tea hangs, it’s the ultimate aesthetic social ritual. If you’re obsessed with cafe-hopping, imagine the vibes of a traditional Chinese tea house. 🫖 Which of the 6 categories are you trying first? Drop a 🍃 if you need recs!
ops_tips: Pair with a high-quality, aesthetic carousel of different tea colors (green, oolong, dark) or a cozy tea-pouring Reel.
Pin a comment listing the 6 tea categories (Green, White, Yellow, Oolong, Black, Dark) to boost engagement and educate.
